summary: Kershaw County, SC: 80-foot steel lookout tower erected by 1932; no source found describes the site today.

facts.design: 80-foot steel lookout tower; OpenStreetMap tags it as a lattice observation tower

events.note: State Commission of Forestry report for Oct 1931 to Sep 1932 says an 80-foot steel tower was erected at Liberty Hill
Tower unit buildings (four-room dwelling, barn, smoke house, chicken house, latrine) built at five tower sites, Liberty Hill among them; report covers July 1937 to June 1938
SC Forestry Commission closed its fire tower system on Oct 1, 1993; the source is system-wide and does not name this tower

notes_for_editor: Record id us-sc-liberty-hill is the Kershaw County tower (OSM 357101767, 34.4757, -80.8035; elevation 173 m matches the record). Do not confuse it with us-sc-liberty-hill-2 (Edgefield County, NHLR US 836): the NHLR Liberty Hill entry and the Augusta Chronicle 2007 hit both concern that other tower. The 80-foot height is the total tower height as quoted from the 1932 report; the cab-floor height is not given. The 1932 and 1937-38 facts are quoted from the Forest Lookouts page, which quotes State Commission of Forestry reports; the reports themselves were not read. The 1993 closure is system-wide and is not tied to this tower in any source. No staffing, fire, or access source was found; no current-status source was found; OSM is volunteer map data, not a site check. No photos found. Research went slightly over the six-read cap, chasing the Edgefield namesake.
